annotation.title_clean: The Information Commissioner v Clearview AI Incorporated
annotation.title_en: The Information Commissioner v Clearview AI Incorporated
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Upper Tribunal (Administrative Appeals Chamber), United Kingdom
annotation.venue: Find Case Law - The National Archives
annotation.summary_en: UK Upper Tribunal decision allowing the Information Commissioner's appeal against Clearview AI. It holds that Clearview's facial-image scraping and biometric database processing falls within the material and territorial scope of the UK and EU GDPR, so the ICO had jurisdiction to issue its notices. The case is remitted to the First-tier Tribunal.
key_provisions_or_claims: Article 2(2)(a) GDPR exclusion covers only activities where Member States reserved control, not all matters outside Union competence.
'Behavioural monitoring' in Article 3(2)(b) is interpreted broadly and includes passive automated collection and classification.
'Related to' in Article 3(2) covers controllers whose processing relates to another controller's behavioural monitoring.
Clearview's processing is not excluded by comity or state-function arguments.
First-tier Tribunal decision set aside and remitted on the basis that the ICO had jurisdiction.
